transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I can handle the technical parts fine, but I just can’t seem to keep all the pieces of these projects organized anymore. Since taking on a lead architect role about a year ago, the sheer volume of moving parts has become really overwhelming to manage.

Did these difficulties start mainly after taking on the lead architect role, or do you also feel persistently anxious, down, or exhausted even outside of work? Have they continued even when work pressure is lower?

While these issues became much harder to manage after my promotion a year ago, they aren't actually new. Looking back, I've had these scattered, detail-losing habits since primary school, where teachers always commented on my careless mistakes. They are a constant struggle even when work pressure is lower, and the resulting mistakes have me really worried about my job security.

Besides work, do you have the same problems with organization, losing track of details, or finishing tasks in other parts of life like home, bills, or relationships? And as a child, were you also often fidgety, impulsive, or told you had trouble paying attention in more than one setting, such as both school and home?

Yes, it definitely spills over; I’ve started forgetting commitments outside of core work, like travel planning, workshop details, and gallery submissions. As a kid, it was an issue at both school and home, where teachers noted my careless mistakes on report cards and my parents had to constantly sit with me just to get me to finish simple homework without drifting off.

Outside of worrying about mistakes or job security, do you find yourself excessively worrying about many different areas of life most days for at least 6 months? If so, is that worry hard to control and accompanied by symptoms like feeling keyed up, muscle tension, irritability, or trouble sleeping?

No, I don't really experience generalized worry about other areas of my life, nor do I have physical symptoms like muscle tension or trouble sleeping. Any anxiety I feel is strictly tied to my work performance and the mistakes I've been making since my promotion.
